title: Harness Reimagines Artifact Management for DevSecOps with New Artifact Registry
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/03/harness-artifact-registry/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1773642345346.jpg"/><p>Harness has announced the general availability of Harness Artifact Registry, a platform capability designed to simplify how engineering teams store, secure, and govern software artifacts within modern DevSecOps pipelines.</p> <i>By Craig Risi</i>

title: QCon London 2026: Kleppmann on Mitigating Europe's Cloud Dependency with Local-First Software
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/03/qcon-local-first-sovereignty/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1773767432899.jpg"/><p>Europe is completely dependent on US cloud services, Martin Kleppmann told QCon London. His fix: commoditise everything. He walked through three technologies he's helped build: multi-cloud via de facto standards, Bluesky's AT Protocol for social media, and local-first software for collaboration, all designed to make switching providers trivial and shift power back to users.</p> <i>By Steef-Jan Wiggers</i>

title: Article: Configuration as a Control Plane: Designing for Safety and Reliability at Scale
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/articles/configuration-control-plane/en/headerimage/configuration-as-a-control-plane-designing-for-safety-and-reliability-at-scale-header-1773657574566.jpg"/><p>Configuration has evolved from static deployment files into a live control plane that directly shapes system behavior. The evolution of configuration management highlights why misconfigurations can trigger large outages and how hyperscalers deploy changes safely using staged rollouts, validation, blast radius limits, and automated rollback at scale.</p> <i>By Karthiek Maralla</i>

title: QCon London 2026: Morgan Stanley Rethinks Its API Program for the MCP Era
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/03/morgan-stanley-apis-mcp-calm/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1773770107168.jpg"/><p>Morgan Stanley engineers Jim Gough and Andreea Niculcea showed how they're retooling the bank's API program for AI agents using MCP and FINOS CALM. Live demos covered compliance guardrails, deployment gates, and zero-downtime rollouts across 100+ APIs. First API deployment shrank from two years to two weeks. They also demoed Google's A2A protocol running alongside MCP.</p> <i>By Steef-Jan Wiggers</i>

title: Microsoft Adds DRA-Backed NVIDIA vGPU Support to AKS
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/03/microsoft-nvidia-gpu/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1773843962447.jpg"/><p>The Azure Kubernetes Service team shared a detailed guide on how to use Dynamic Resource Allocation (DRA) with NVIDIA vGPU technology on AKS. his update improves control and efficiency for shared GPU use in AI and media tasks.</p> <i>By Claudio Masolo</i>

title: QCon London 2026: Wrangling Telemetry at Scale, a Guide to Self-Hosted Observability
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/03/self-hosted-observability/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1773862581289.jpg"/><p>At QCon London 2026, Colin Douch discussed building and operating self-hosted monitoring stacks, surveyed the current tooling landscape, and explained how to build a coherent observability setup rather than treating logs, metrics, and traces as separate pillars.</p> <i>By Renato Losio</i>

title: QCon London 2026: SBOMs Move From Best Practice to Legal Obligation as CRA Enforcement Looms
War in Iran Damages Multiple AWS Data Centers, Challenging Multi-AZ Assumptions
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/03/aws-multiaz-conflict-outage/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1773671194784.jpg"/><p>Earlier this month, Iranian drone strikes damaged three AWS data centers in the UAE and Bahrain, causing outages and disruptions to multiple services. The events, which affected multiple facilities within the same AWS region, sparked discussion in the community about how geopolitical conflict can directly impact global cloud infrastructure and multi-AZ deployments.</p> <i>By Renato Losio</i>

title: QCon London 2026: Uncorking Queueing Bottlenecks with OpenTelemetry
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/03/queue-otel-observability/en/headerimage/header-1773741090866.jpeg"/><p>At QCon London 2026, Julian Wreford and Oli Lane from Gearset showcased how distributed tracing and SLOs solve asynchronous observability gaps. By shifting from queue-size metrics to latency-based alerts, the team improved incident response. Key technical takeaways included using OpenTelemetry trace state for async duration tracking and wide events to uncover hidden architectural waste.</p> <i>By Mark Silvester</i>

title: QCon London 2026: Shipping Constantly with Humans and Beyond at Monzo
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/03/shipping-monzo/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1773761561765.jpg"/><p>At QCon London 2026, Suhail Patel, a principal engineer at Monzo who leads the bank’s platform group, described how the bank has built a developer platform capable of shipping hundreds of changes to production every day.</p> <i>By Matt Saunders</i>

title: QCon London 2026: Your Multi-Cloud Strategy Is a Product Problem — Treat It Like One
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/03/jpmc-multicloud-product-strategy/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1773667022672.jpg"/><p>JP Morgan Chase engineers Luis Albinati and Surabhi Mahajan argued that multi-cloud complexity can't be solved with engineering alone. Speaking at QCon London, they showed how treating multi-cloud as a product with capability mapping, demand governance, and defined users tames the chaos.</p> <i>By Steef-Jan Wiggers</i>

title: AI Is Amplifying Software Engineering Performance, Says the 2025 DORA Report
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/03/ai-dora-report/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1773641593696.jpg"/><p>Artificial intelligence is rapidly reshaping the way software is built, but its impact is more nuanced than many organizations expected. The 2025 DevOps Research and Assessment (DORA) report, titled State of AI-Assisted Software Development, finds that AI does not automatically improve software delivery performance.</p> <i>By Craig Risi</i>

title: QCon London 2026: How to Run on Three Clouds at Once, and When Not to
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/03/form3-triple-active-multicloud/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1773663355236.jpg"/><p>Form3 runs UK bank payments across three clouds simultaneously. At QCon London, their engineers explained how they built their custom Kubernetes operators, cross-cloud DNS tricks, and distributed databases, and what happened when they tried to sell them in America. Spoiler: US customers wanted East/West failover, not triple-active multi-cloud.</p> <i>By Steef-Jan Wiggers</i>

title: AWS Launches Managed Openclaw on Lightsail amid Critical Security Vulnerabilities
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/03/aws-lightsail-openclaw-security/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1772738153368.jpg"/><p>AWS launched managed OpenClaw on Lightsail for AI agent deployment while security concerns mount. The 250k-star GitHub project is affected by CVE-2026-25253, which enables one-click RCE, with 17,500+ vulnerable instances exposed. Bitdefender found 20% of ClawHub skills malicious. AWS blueprint provides automated hardening, but doesn't address architectural security limits.</p> <i>By Steef-Jan Wiggers</i>

title: Elastic Releases Version 9.3.0 with Enhanced AI Tools and OTel Support
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/03/elastic-9-3-gpu-vector-indexing/en/headerimage/header-1772835595760.jpeg"/><p>Elastic 9.3.0 is now available, featuring enhanced vector search indexing for RAG applications and significant upgrades to the ES|QL query language. The release deepens OpenTelemetry integration for vendor-neutral observability and updates the AI Assistant with better contextual analysis. Security visibility is also expanded across Kubernetes and serverless architectures.</p> <i>By Mark Silvester</i>
